body:
@jeffbcross could you take a look at this ? 

How is this tested in the http module ?

@thelgevold well it's not an issue with the header, it's the `JSON.stringify()` which makes your example work. If that's what we're supposed to do now, it's a breaking change, as it wasn't required in RC4.

Prior to rc.2, it was required to add the header and stringify yourself.
This [commit](https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/0f0a8ade7cc7021ae17a69e1bf1222378f7aaefb) in rc.2 handles JSON for object payloads.
Looks like current master broke it with [this commit](https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/e7a8e2757b06d572f614f53b648d2fd75df370d2).

@vicb  This is tested here : 
(angular/modules/@angular/http/test/backends/xhr_backend_spec.ts line 259)
`expect(sendSpy).toHaveBeenCalledWith(body);`

Which should become :
`expect(sendSpy).toHaveBeenCalledWith(JSON.stringify(body));` 
If we intend to convert json objects to string when there are passed as the request body.

If you want a fix for that, let me know.

@cassand yep a PR would be great, thanks.

We also probably need to fire up a server for the tests but that you be yet another PR.

issue.title: fix(http): convert objects passed to requests into a string

**What is the current behavior?**
When an object is passed to a request, no modification occurs on that object and therefore is converted to `[object Object]`

Refer to this issue : [#10073](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/10073)

**What is the new behavior?**

Now objects passed to requests are converted to a string (which was the default behavior in RC4)

**Does this PR introduce a breaking change?** (check one with "x")

This remove a breaking change introduced with this [commit](https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/7260) 

**Other information**:

This remove a breaking change introduced with [commit](https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/7260)  where json objects passed to  requests were not converted into string.
Refer to issue : #10073
